column14: It can survive outdoors, but I placed it inside an unheated greenhouse shelf after it's first winter for it to grow faster.
column38: It survived its first seedling age (when it was just 3-4 months old) outdoor in the rainy and cold winter climate with no protection.

It was germinated in the peak of winter indoor, and brought outside to the unheated greenhouse shelf during late winter. It was brought outside with no more greenhouse protection after spring came, and stayed there ever since. I had 13 seeds and only two germinated, and the other seedling died at the unheated greenhouse shelf phase. This seedling is the only survivor till now.

It is growing vegetatively very vigorously for a pomegranate plant in my city where most pomegranate varieties struggle to grow or fruit. Even though most pomegranate varieties have a hard time fruiting in my climate, the germination rate for the seeds I planted was relatively high but with a small sample size of 2 out of 3.
